question.problem: Starting with the standard Maclaurin expansion for $\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion for $\int \sqrt{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x.$

current_example.problem: Starting with the standard Maclaurin result for $e^x,$ find the first three terms of the series expansion for $\displaystyle{\int e^{-x^2}\textrm{d}x}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The series expansion of $e^{x}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & =1+x+\frac{1}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-x^2$ in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-{x}^{2}} & =1+(-{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{2!}(-{x}^{2})^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, integrating with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {e}^{-{x}^{2}}\text{d}x & =\int (1-{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =C+x-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{10}{x}^{5}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
